subject: Medford School Committee Compensation
overview: The committee discussed several proposals to increase School Committee pay for the first time in 23 years, weighing the goal of equitable representation against strong opposition from school staff regarding the district's budget crisis. Four competing motions regarding salary phase-ins and automatic review mechanisms were referred to the regular council meeting or specific committees.

items.title: Legal Opinion on Compensation Adjustments
items.summary: Legal counsel provided an opinion stating that a simple majority vote of the City Council is required to change school committee compensation for the next fiscal year, while a two-thirds vote would be necessary for mid-year supplemental appropriations.

items.title: School Committee Salary Comparison and Data
items.summary: Councilor Tseng presented data comparing the current $12,000 school committee stipend to inflation, city council increases, and teacher contract adjustments since the year 2000.

items.title: Public Participation on School Funding and Salaries
items.summary: Teachers, union representatives, and parents spoke against substantial raises for elected officials, citing underfunded school buildings, low paraprofessional wages, and stagnant stipends for coaches.

items.title: Four-Year Phase-In to Council Parity
items.summary: The committee referred a proposal to phase in school committee raises over four years, reaching parity with city council salaries by 2027, to the regular meeting.

items.title: Two-Year MTA-Indexed Phase-In
items.summary: A motion to increase committee pay over two years to match the historical growth rates of teacher contracts was referred to the regular meeting.

items.title: Referral for Automatic Compensation Review
items.summary: The committee referred a resolution to the Governance Committee to consider a charter mechanism for automatic cost-of-living adjustments for all elected officials.

items.title: Council Salary Reduction Proposal
items.summary: The committee referred a motion to lower city council pay to a blended rate with the school committee to ensure legislative pay equity without increasing the total budget.
